cancel-an-order.author: founder
cancel-an-order.body:
With issues like these, we should ask the customer if we can refund them and they can cancel the disputes, as it gives multiple charges to us as a company. But with the initial response that this person gave—that they did not place an order—we cannot physically place an order for anyone. So it means that when somebody says something like this, we should ask them to check if a family member or something might have placed it. Maybe they are old and forgot , but likely a family member placed the order or they are lying because they have regret of spending money

But if they wish to cancel it and it's happened before the order's fulfilled, usually being a 24-hour period from when they ordered, then we can cancel and refund them. That's our standard procedure. If it's been fulfilled, we inform them: we can't cancel the order, but when you receive the order, we can work on a return and just tell them to email us as soon as it arrives.

Once we've fulfilled it, we can't change it from our side. Most people don't come back after they receive the product and say they want to still exchange it. It's a good way of dealing with those types of customers.

You are not supposed to add that last bit of text in your email where you said, "that's it." If you'd still prefer a refund after that, we're happy to take care of it. I know that's how Claude usually defaults to respond, but when you put that at the end, everybody's going to take the refund. So don't say that.

And then if people still push back, then you offer the refund. The way that you had worded the message at first was good. Yeah, just don't have that at the end of the message because psychologically everyone is going to take the refund there.

And this is not a refund-worthy order because now they're saying full refund, and it's not a full refund order. It's if they didn't want an exchange, the best you can do is a 50% refund. So please see if you can, yeah, just speak to them and say that it will be a 50% refund, but just try to find the best way to word it.

Potentially say that our policy only allows free shade exchanges right now for our perfect match promise, but you managed to get her situation addressed. Don't actually mention manager. Just say that because she's unhappy, you will give her a 50% refund, but it's against our policies.  When you say that it's against our policies, don't forget to say it. I'm not telling you to say it—I'm saying to mention it, because then it feels like you made a concession and she'll feel better about it.
